10.text:
[Verse 1]
To make a promise, start with "I'll."
I'll call you after class.

For what you promise you won't do, sing "I won't."
I won't be late tomorrow.

To ask about tomorrow, start "will you?"
Will you join us tomorrow?

For a plan you made, sing "I'm going to."
I'm going to practice English tonight.

[Chorus]
Tomorrow's on my mind tonight.
My plans can change before it's light.
A time, a place, a thing to do.
Tomorrow's song is coming through.

[Verse 2]
For what you plan to avoid, sing "I'm not going to."
I'm not going to skip breakfast.

To ask about a plan, use "are you going to?"
Are you going to study tonight?

For what you're planning, sing "I'm planning to."
I'm planning to learn ten new words.

For a meeting that's arranged, name who and when.
I'm meeting my friends at six.

[Verse 3]
For a set timetable, use the simple present.
The class starts at nine tomorrow.

For something you hope will happen, sing "I hope to."
I hope to learn English well.

When you're still unsure, sing "I might."
I might go to the park after lunch.

[Chorus]
Tomorrow's on my mind tonight.
My plans can change before it's light.
A time, a place, a thing to do.
Tomorrow's song is coming through.

scenes.context: قد أذهب إلى الحديقة بعد الغداء.

translations.7: لتسأل عن الغد، ابدأ بـ «هل ستفعل؟».
translations.15: قد تتغيّر خططي قبل طلوع النهار.
translations.20: لشيء تنوي تجنّبه، غنِّ «لا أنوي أن».
translations.23: لتسأل عن خطة، قل «هل تنوي أن؟».
translations.29: للقاء رتّبته، اذكر مع من ومتى.

translations.40: قد أذهب إلى الحديقة بعد الغداء.
translations.44: قد تتغيّر خططي قبل طلوع النهار.

11.text:
[Verse 1]
Name the way you feel with "I feel."
I feel calm after my walk.

If you're pleased with a result, sing "I'm happy with."
I'm happy with my test result.

To name a worry, sing "I'm worried about."
I'm worried about missing the bus.

For a subject you want to explore, sing "I'm interested in."
I'm interested in learning new languages.

[Chorus]
Hear me out and hear my side.
We can let two thoughts collide.
One for how, and one for why.
Let them meet and let them fly.

[Verse 2]
To share a thought, sing "I think."
I think this lesson is useful.

To share their view, sing "I agree with."
I agree with your suggestion.

For a different view, sing "I don't agree with."
I don't agree with that idea.

To tell how much time you need, sing "it takes."
It takes ten minutes to get there.

[Verse 3]
To give the reason, sing "because."
I practice English because I want to travel.

To give the result, sing "so."
We were hungry, so we made lunch.

To give the purpose, use "to" and a verb.
I opened the book to check the answer.

When ideas pull apart, join them with "but."
The test was hard, but I passed.

[Chorus]
Hear me out and hear my side.
We can let two thoughts collide.
One for how, and one for why.
Let them meet and let them fly.

translations.4: إذا أسعدتك نتيجة، غنِّ «أنا سعيد بـ».
translations.7: لتذكر ما يقلقك، غنِّ «أنا قلق بشأن».
translations.10: لموضوع تريد استكشافه، غنِّ «أنا مهتمّ بـ».
translations.14: اسمعني إلى النهاية واسمع وجهة نظري.
translations.23: لتوافق شخصًا على رأيه، غنِّ «أتفق مع».
translations.26: للتعبير عن رأي مختلف، غنِّ «لا أتفق مع».
translations.30: يستغرق الوصول إلى هناك عشر دقائق.
translations.34: أتدرب على الإنجليزية لأنني أريد السفر.
translations.39: لتذكر الغاية، استخدم to ثم فعلًا.
translations.46: اسمعني إلى النهاية واسمع وجهة نظري.

12.text:
[Verse 1]
For an old habit you've left behind, sing "I used to."
I used to walk to school.

For an action going on then, sing "I was" with an "ing" verb.
I was reading at eight o'clock.

Use "while" when something happens during another action.
While I was reading, the phone rang.

Use "when" to connect two moments in the past.
When I opened the door, I saw a cat.

[Chorus]
Yesterday is bound to fade.
Tomorrow's plans are being made.
If it rains or if it's clear,
I'll be ready when it's here.

[Verse 2]
For an outcome you think is likely, sing "I expect to."
I expect to arrive before sunset.

For something that might happen, sing "I may."
I may need my umbrella this afternoon.

For what you'll likely do, sing "I'll probably."
I'll probably take the early bus.

When it's almost time to act, sing "I'm about to."
I'm about to leave the house.

[Verse 3]
For a possible condition and its result, sing "if," then "I'll."
If it rains, I'll stay at home.

For a future time, use "when," then "I'll" for the result.
When I get home, I'll call my mother.

For something you'll do right after an event, start "as soon as."
As soon as I finish, I'll help you.

[Chorus]
Yesterday is bound to fade.
Tomorrow's plans are being made.
If it rains or if it's clear,
I'll be ready when it's here.

13.text:
[Verse 1]
To celebrate an achievement, sing "I'm proud of."
I'm proud of my progress in English.

When something catches you off guard, sing "I'm surprised that."
I'm surprised that the shop is open.

When things fall short, sing "I'm disappointed that."
I'm disappointed that the game was canceled.

[Chorus]
Some days I smile, some days I don't.
Some things I'll choose, some things I won't.
In my own words, I'll let you know
What I feel and where I'll go.

[Verse 2]
To show what you're thankful for, sing "I'm grateful for."
I'm grateful for your kindness.

To say what you want to do right now, sing "I feel like."
I feel like going for a walk.

If you're not in the mood, sing "I don't feel like."
I don't feel like watching TV.

[Verse 3]
To mark a view as yours, sing "in my opinion."
In my opinion, we need more practice.

For a view you hold, sing "I believe."
I believe everyone can learn.

To compare what you like, use "I prefer," then "to."
I prefer walking to driving.

[Chorus]
Some days I smile, some days I don't.
Some things I'll choose, some things I won't.
In my own words, I'll let you know
What I feel and where I'll go.

14.text:
[Verse 1]
For an impression you're still checking, sing "it seems like."
It seems like the shop is closed.

For a guess based on what you hear, sing "it sounds like."
It sounds like rain outside.

Ask them to act with "would you mind" and an "ing" verb.
Would you mind moving your bag?

[Chorus]
Hear me out, and I'll hear you.
A little care comes shining through.
Take a breath and make it clear.
You've got a voice I want to hear.

[Verse 2]
To ask before you act, sing "do you mind if I?"
Do you mind if I sit here?

To turn something down kindly, sing "I'm afraid I can't."
I'm afraid I can't come on Friday.

To show that you value something, sing "I appreciate."
I appreciate your patience today.

[Verse 3]
If the meaning isn't clear, ask "could you clarify?"
Could you clarify what you mean?

Ask to hear if something happens, sing "let me know if."
Let me know if the time changes.

[Chorus]
Hear me out, and I'll hear you.
A little care comes shining through.
Take a breath and make it clear.
You've got a voice I want to hear.

15.text:
[Verse 1]
Before a noun that gives the cause, sing "because of."
The bus was late because of traffic.

After the reason, lead to the result with "that's why."
I missed the bus. That's why I'm late.

To explain what you want to make possible, sing "so that."
I write notes so that I can remember more.

[Chorus]
Join the lines and let them flow.
Show me where your thoughts can go.
Give me one and give me two.
Now I see your point of view.

[Verse 2]
Start with "although" when two ideas pull apart.
Although she was tired, she kept studying.

Start a new sentence with "however" to show a contrast.
The book is long. However, it is easy to read.

When one thing takes another's place, sing "instead of."
She chose water instead of soda.

[Verse 3]
For a case that shows your point, sing "for example."
Healthy habits help us. For example, sleep improves focus.

To name examples within a group, sing "such as."
I enjoy fruits such as apples and oranges.

To make your point more clear, sing "what I mean is."
What I mean is we need more practice.

[Chorus]
Join the lines and let them flow.
Show me where your thoughts can go.
Give me one and give me two.
Now I see your point of view.

16.text:
[Verse 1]
To introduce your reason, sing "the reason is that."
The reason is that the library closes early.

To wonder about a yes or no, use "if" with statement word order.
I wonder if the museum is open today.

To wonder how, keep the subject before its verb.
I wonder how this machine works.

[Chorus]
I wonder where, I wonder how.
Let's find a little answer now.
A person, a place, a thing to see.
The pieces fit when you sing with me.

[Verse 2]
Add "who" to show which person you mean.
The person who helped me is my neighbor.

Add "that" to show which thing you mean.
The song that we heard was beautiful.

Add "where" to show which place you mean.
She works at the café where we met last summer.

[Verse 3]
When you succeed after a try, sing "I managed to."
I managed to finish on time.

For something that deserves the effort, sing "it's worth" plus an "ing" verb.
It's worth trying again.

After "do you know where," put the subject before the verb.
Do you know where the station is?

[Chorus]
I wonder where, I wonder how.
Let's find a little answer now.
A person, a place, a thing to see.
The pieces fit when you sing with me.

17.text:
[Verse 1]
For a surprising result despite a fact, sing "even though."
Even though it was raining, we went outside.

To set two different views side by side, sing "while."
While I enjoy reading, my brother prefers sports.

To add something more, sing "in addition to."
In addition to English, I study mathematics.

[Chorus]
Even if the sky turns gray,
We'll find words to guide the way.
Give each thought its time to land.
Sing it till you understand.

[Verse 2]
For two points in balance, sing "not only" and "but also."
He is not only helpful but also patient.

To name the exception to a plan, sing "unless."
We'll go outside unless it rains.

If a possible obstacle wouldn't change your plan, sing "even if."
Even if it rains, I'll attend the event.

[Verse 3]
To name what counts the most, sing "what matters is."
What matters is that we keep trying.

After "could you tell me whether," put the subject first.
Could you tell me whether the office is open?

[Chorus]
Even if the sky turns gray,
We'll find words to guide the way.
Give each thought its time to land.
Sing it till you understand.

18.text:
[Verse 1]
To say which day you remember, add "when."
I still think about the day when I started school.

For an ability you wish you had, sing "I wish I could."
I wish I could play the piano well.

Picture a world that's different now. Sing "if I were," then "I would."
If I were a teacher, I would make lessons fun.

[Chorus]
Days behind us, words to keep.
Some are light and some go deep.
Looking back, I learn to see
What was and what could be.

[Verse 2]
For an unreal past and its result, sing "if I had," then "would have."
If I had left early, I would have caught the bus.

For a better choice you missed, sing "I should have."
I should have brought my umbrella.

For an option you had back then, sing "I could have."
I could have taken the earlier bus.

[Verse 3]
For what was done before another past event, sing "I had already."
I had already eaten when my friend called.

Set a point in the past with "by the time," then say what had happened.
By the time she called, I had finished cooking.

When two things change together, sing "the more" twice."
We find that the more we practice, the more confident we become.

[Chorus]
Days behind us, words to keep.
Some are light and some go deep.
Looking back, I learn to see
What was and what could be.

translations.28: كنت قد تناولت الطعام عندما اتصل صديقي.
translations.30: حدّد لحظة في الماضي بقول «بحلول الوقت الذي»، ثم اذكر ما كان قد حدث.
translations.31: بحلول اتصالها، كنت قد أنهيت الطبخ.
translations.33: عندما يتغيّر شيئان معًا، غنِّ «كلما» للمقارنة بينهما.
translations.34: نجد أنه كلما تدربنا أكثر، أصبحنا أكثر ثقة.
translations.37: أيام مضت وكلمات تستحق أن تبقى.
translations.39: حين أنظر إلى الوراء، أتعلّم أن أرى
translations.40: ما كان وما كان يمكن أن يكون.

01.text:
[Verse 1]
To tell your name, start like this.
My name is Ali.

To ask my name, sing it back.
What's your name?

To say who you are, start with "I'm."
I'm a student.

One thing near you, say "this is."
This is my house.

[Chorus]
Hello, hello, come sing with me.
A name, a face, a thing to see.
Near or far, just look around.
One little line, one little sound.

[Verse 2]
One thing farther, say "that is."
That is my house.

To talk about the weather, sing "it is."
It is cold.

To ask about a thing, use "what."
What is this word?

[Verse 3]
To ask about a person, use "who."
Who is at the door?

For things you have, sing "I have."
I have two books.

For something you want, sing "I want."
I want some water.

[Chorus]
Hello, hello, come sing with me.
A name, a face, a thing to see.
Near or far, just look around.
One little line, one little sound.

translations.4: ولتسألني عن اسمي، غنِّ السؤال بدورك.
translations.10: للإشارة إلى شيء قريب منك، قل «هذا».
translations.16: قريبًا كان أو بعيدًا، انظر حولك.
translations.42: قريبًا كان أو بعيدًا، انظر حولك.

02.text:
[Verse 1]
To ask nicely for a thing, try "I'd like."
I'd like a sandwich.

To ask if you may, try "can I?"
Can I sit here?

A little "please" makes a request kind.
Speak slowly, please.

To ask someone to act, try "can you?"
Can you open the window?

[Chorus]
One small word can open a door.
One kind voice can tell you more.
Ask it once, and let it ring.
Hear how easy it is to sing.

[Verse 2]
To get someone's attention, try "excuse me."
Excuse me, where is the library?

To ask for a place, try "where is?"
Where is the bus stop?

One thing is here, so sing "there is."
There is a book on the table.

For things right here, sing "these are."
These are my books.

[Verse 3]
More than one? Sing "there are."
There are three chairs here.

To ask if one is here, try "is there?"
Is there a book on the table?

To ask if any are here, try "are there?"
Are there any seats available?

[Chorus]
One small word can open a door.
One kind voice can tell you more.
Ask it once, and let it ring.
Hear how easy it is to sing.

translations.10: لتطلب من شخص فعل شيء، جرّب «هل يمكنك؟».
translations.26: إذا كان هنا شيء واحد، فغنِّ «يوجد».
translations.33: أكثر من شيء؟ غنِّ صيغة الجمع «توجد أشياء».
translations.36: لتسأل عن وجود شيء واحد، جرّب «هل يوجد؟».
translations.39: لتسأل عن وجود عدة أشياء، جرّب «هل توجد؟».

03.text:
[Verse 1]
For water or a price, ask "how much?"
How much water do you need?

For things you can count, ask "how many?"
How many apples do you want?

For a thing you need, sing "I need."
I need a pencil.

To say what you want to do, add "to."
I want to learn English.

[Chorus]
Count the apples, pour the tea.
Tell me what you need from me.
Say what you like, say what you do.
I'll sing a line, then it's your cue.

[Verse 2]
Say what you'd like to do, politely.
I'd like to order lunch.

When someone thanks you, here's your reply.
You're welcome. I'm happy to help.

For something you enjoy, sing "I like."
I like reading.

[Verse 3]
For something you don't enjoy, sing "I don't like."
I don't like cold weather.

Tell me what you're able to do.
I can ride a bike.

Tell me what you can't do.
I can't hear you clearly.

[Chorus]
Count the apples, pour the tea.
Tell me what you need from me.
Say what you like, say what you do.
I'll sing a line, then it's your cue.

translations.1: للسؤال عن كمية الماء أو السعر، قل «كم؟».
translations.4: للأشياء التي يمكن عدّها، اسأل «كم عددها؟».
translations.7: للحديث عن شيء تحتاج إليه، غنِّ «أحتاج إلى».
translations.10: لتذكر ما تريد فعله، ضع to قبل الفعل.
translations.16: قل ما تحب وقل ما تفعل.
translations.30: للحديث عما لا تستمتع به، غنِّ «لا أحبّ».
translations.36: قل لي ما لا تستطيع فعله.
translations.42: قل ما تحب وقل ما تفعل.

04.text:
[Verse 1]
To suggest we do it together, sing "let's."
Let's go to the park.

To offer someone something, try "would you like?"
Would you like some tea?

To ask the time or date, start "when is?"
When is your birthday?

To ask how something is, start "how is?"
How is the weather today?

[Chorus]
Come along, the day is new.
I've got a song to share with you.
Step by step and line by line,
Sing with me and keep in time.

[Verse 2]
Ask about a habit with "do you."
Do you like apples?

Name the place you go to.
I go to work by bus.

When sleep is done, you wake up.
I wake up at six.

[Verse 3]
When you leave your bed, you get up.
I get up at six thirty.

For what you do early in the day, sing "in the morning."
In the morning, I drink water.

To talk about brushing, here's what to say.
I brush my teeth every morning.

[Chorus]
Come along, the day is new.
I've got a song to share with you.
Step by step and line by line,
Sing with me and keep in time.

scenes.context: أنهض من السرير الساعة السادسة والنصف.

translations.1: لتقترح أن نفعل شيئًا معًا، غنِّ «هيا بنا».
translations.4: لتعرض شيئًا على شخص، جرّب «هل تودّ؟».
translations.10: لتسأل عن حال شيء، ابدأ بـ «كيف؟».
translations.20: للسؤال عن عادة، ابدأ بـ «هل تفعل؟».
translations.31: أنهض من السرير الساعة السادسة والنصف.
translations.33: للحديث عمّا تفعله باكرًا، غنِّ «في الصباح».
translations.36: للحديث عن تنظيف الأسنان، إليك ما تقول.

05.text:
[Verse 1]
To talk about your first meal, sing "I have breakfast."
I have breakfast at seven.

To say what you have for a meal, sing "I eat."
I eat an apple after school.

If you do it daily, sing "every day."
I practice English every day.

When the sky gets dark, sing "at night."
At night, I read a short story.

[Chorus]
Day by day, the hours go by.
Breakfast first and stars at night.
Some things change and some things stay.
This is how I sing my day.

[Verse 2]
When it's time to sleep, say "I go to bed."
I go to bed at nine.

For habits you have each weekend, sing "on weekends."
I play football on weekends.

What you do most times, you "usually" do.
I usually walk to school.

If you do it every time, sing "always."
I always say good morning.

[Verse 3]
If you do it many times, sing "often."
I often go to the library.

If you do it now and then, sing "sometimes."
I sometimes walk to work.

If it never happens, sing "I never."
I never skip breakfast.

[Chorus]
Day by day, the hours go by.
Breakfast first and stars at night.
Some things change and some things stay.
This is how I sing my day.

scenes.context: ألعب كرة القدم في عطلة نهاية الأسبوع.

translations.1: للحديث عن أول وجبة، غنِّ «أتناول الفطور».
translations.7: إذا كنت تفعله يوميًا، غنِّ «كل يوم».
translations.20: حين يحين وقت النوم، قل «أذهب إلى الفراش».
translations.23: لعادات نهاية الأسبوع، غنِّ «في عطلة نهاية الأسبوع».
translations.24: ألعب كرة القدم في عطلة نهاية الأسبوع.
translations.29: إذا كنت تفعله كل مرة، غنِّ «دائمًا».
translations.33: إذا كنت تفعله مرات كثيرة، غنِّ «غالبًا».
translations.36: إذا فعلته بين الحين والآخر، غنِّ «أحيانًا».
translations.39: إذا لم يحدث قط، فغنِّ «لا أفعل أبدًا».

06.text:
[Verse 1]
Another way to say you have it.
I've got a ticket.

For an action you need, sing "I need to."
I need to catch the bus.

For something required, sing "I have to."
I have to study for my exam.

If it's up to you, sing "I don't have to."
I don't have to work today.

[Chorus]
What have I got? What should I do?
I've got a choice, and so have you.
A little help, a little time,
And I can find the next right line.

[Verse 2]
When you really have to, sing "I must."
I must wear my seat belt.

Advice for myself starts with "I should."
I should practice more.

Advice for you starts with "you should."
You should take a short break.

[Verse 3]
To offer to do it yourself, sing "let me."
Let me help you.

To check if a plan is okay, sing "is it okay if?"
Is it okay if we sit here?

To give permission, say "you may."
You may use this computer.

[Chorus]
What have I got? What should I do?
I've got a choice, and so have you.
A little help, a little time,
And I can find the next right line.

translations.1: إليك طريقة أخرى لتقول إن الشيء لديك.

translations.7: للتعبير عمّا يلزمك فعله، غنِّ «عليّ أن».
translations.10: إذا كان القرار لك، غنِّ «لست مضطرًا إلى أن».
translations.14: ماذا لديّ؟ وماذا ينبغي أن أفعل؟
translations.16: بشيء من المساعدة وقليل من الوقت،
translations.20: حين يكون الفعل واجبًا حقًا، غنِّ «يجب عليّ».
translations.23: تبدأ نصيحتي لنفسي بـ «ينبغي لي أن».
translations.26: وتبدأ نصيحتي لك بـ «ينبغي لك أن».
translations.33: لتتأكد من أن خطتك مقبولة، غنِّ «هل لا بأس إن…؟».
translations.34: هل من المقبول إذا جلسنا هنا؟
translations.40: ماذا لديّ؟ وماذا ينبغي أن أفعل؟
translations.42: بشيء من المساعدة وقليل من الوقت،

07.text:
[Verse 1]
To invite someone to act, sing "would you like to?"
Would you like to join us?

For a polite request, start "could you please."
Could you please repeat the last sentence?

For a more formal request, sing "may I?"
May I come in, please?

Say yes with a smile, sing "I'd love to."
I'd love to join the trip.

[Chorus]
Come and join us, stay awhile.
Ask a question, share a smile.
Kind words travel to and fro.
Where they land, a friendship grows.

[Verse 2]
Make a suggestion with "how about?"
How about meeting at the library?

To name what you are thankful for, sing "thank you for."
Thank you for waiting for me.

To apologize for an action, sing "I'm sorry for."
I'm sorry for being late today.

To tell them it's okay, sing "that's all right."
That's all right. We can try again.

[Verse 3]
Use "what do you" to ask what someone does.
What do you do after school?

Use "where do you" to ask where they do it.
Where do you study English?

Use "when do you" to ask when they do it.
When do you practice English?

[Chorus]
Come and join us, stay awhile.
Ask a question, share a smile.
Kind words travel to and fro.
Where they land, a friendship grows.

translations.4: لطلب مهذب، ابدأ بـ «هل يمكنك من فضلك؟».
translations.5: هل يمكنك إعادة الجملة الأخيرة من فضلك؟
translations.7: لطلب أكثر رسمية، غنِّ «هل تسمح لي؟».
translations.8: هل تسمح لي بالدخول من فضلك؟
translations.21: ما رأيك في اللقاء في المكتبة؟
translations.23: لتذكر ما تشكر عليه، غنِّ «شكرًا لك على».
translations.33: اسأل عمّا يفعله شخص باستخدام «ماذا تفعل؟».
translations.36: اسأل عن مكان فعله باستخدام «أين تفعل ذلك؟».
translations.39: اسأل عن وقت فعله باستخدام «متى تفعل ذلك؟».

08.text:
[Verse 1]
To ask why something is that way, start "why is."
Why is the bus late?

To ask why someone does it, start "why do you."
Why do you study English?

To ask how it's done, start "how do you."
How do you make tea?

To ask about her habit, start "does she."
Does she speak English?

[Chorus]
One more question on the way.
One more thing to learn today.
Ask me how and ask me why.
Hear the words and give them a try.

[Verse 2]
When you have a choice, ask "which one?"
Which one should I choose?

Check first, then leave. Hear the word "before."
Before I leave, I check my bag.

Study first, then rest. Hear the word "after."
After I study, I take a break.

[Verse 3]
To say where you were, start "I was."
I was at home yesterday.

To say how you didn't feel, sing "I wasn't."
I wasn't tired yesterday.

To ask where you were, start "were you?"
Were you at school yesterday?

[Chorus]
One more question on the way.
One more thing to learn today.
Ask me how and ask me why.
Hear the words and give them a try.

translations.1: لتسأل عن سبب حال شيء، ابدأ بـ «لماذا هذا…؟».
translations.4: لتسأل شخصًا عن سبب فعله، ابدأ بـ «لماذا تفعل؟».
translations.7: لتسأل عن كيفية فعل شيء، ابدأ بـ «كيف تفعل؟».
translations.10: لتسأل عن عادتها، ابدأ بـ «هل تفعل؟».
translations.20: عندما تكون أمام خيارات، اسأل «أيّ واحد؟».
translations.23: تحقّق أولًا، ثم غادر. اسمع كلمة «قبل».
translations.26: ادرس أولًا، ثم استرح. اسمع كلمة «بعد».
translations.33: لتقول كيف لم تكن تشعر، غنِّ «لم أكن».
translations.36: لتسأل أين كان شخص، ابدأ بـ «هل كنت؟».

09.text:
[Verse 1]
Tell where you went with "I went."
I went to the market yesterday.

For a past action you didn't do, use "didn't" and the plain verb.
I didn't see your message.

For a past question, use "did" and the plain verb.
Did you finish your homework?

For things you once had, sing "I had."
I had a red bicycle as a child.

[Chorus]
Turn the page to yesterday.
Little things can find a way
Back into a song I know.
Where I went and who said hello.

[Verse 2]
Tell what you saw with "I saw."
I saw a rainbow after the rain.

Tell who you met with "I met."
I met an old friend at the market.

Tell what you bought with "I bought."
I bought bread this morning.

Tell what you made with "I made."
I made a paper boat.

[Verse 3]
For something you forgot to do, sing "I forgot to."
I forgot to bring my book.

For a choice you made, sing "I decided to."
I decided to learn English.

To say you began an action, sing "I started."
I started reading a story yesterday.

[Chorus]
Turn the page to yesterday.
Little things can find a way
Back into a song I know.
Where I went and who said hello.

translations.11: كانت لدي دراجة حمراء في طفولتي.

translations.46: أين ذهبت ومن قال لي مرحبًا.
